<div class="guide">

<h3>Gene set enrichment analysis of GO terms and KEGG pathways</h3>
<p class="guide-lead">Start from a table of differential expression results and find the GO terms and KEGG pathways whose genes sit together at the top or the bottom of the ranking. No R programming is needed.</p>
<p class="guide-sub">The analysis is run by <a href="https://bioconductor.org/packages/release/bioc/html/clusterProfiler.html" target="_blank">clusterProfiler</a>. GSEA uses all your genes, ranked by log2 fold change, so there is no significance cutoff to choose and small coordinated changes can still be detected.</p>

<h3>How it works</h3>
<p class="guide-sub">The result tabs appear in the sidebar once the enrichment has run.</p>
<div class="guide-grid">
<div class="guide-card"><h4><span class="guide-step">1</span>Input data</h4><p>Upload a results table, start from the example data, or arrive from DESeq2 Shiny with a comparison already loaded.</p></div>
<div class="guide-card"><h4><span class="guide-step">2</span>Select genes</h4><p>Choose the gene identifier column and the log2 fold change column that ranks the genes.</p></div>
<div class="guide-card"><h4><span class="guide-step">3</span>Enrichment parameters</h4><p>Choose the organism, the key type of your gene identifiers and the ontology, then create the gseGO object.</p></div>
<div class="guide-card"><h4><span class="guide-step">4</span>Explore</h4><p>Browse the gseGO and gseKEGG tables, plot the terms you care about, and download tables and figures.</p></div>
</div>

<h3>What you get</h3>
<p class="guide-sub">Figures from the example data. Click a figure to enlarge it.</p>
<div class="guide-grid guide-plots">
<figure class="guide-figure"><a class="pop"><img src="www/dotplot.png" alt="Dot plot"/></a><figcaption><strong>Dot plot</strong><br/>Enriched terms with their gene ratio and significance.</figcaption></figure>
<figure class="guide-figure"><a class="pop"><img src="www/ridgeplot.png" alt="Ridge plot"/></a><figcaption><strong>Ridge plot</strong><br/>The fold change distribution of the genes in each term.</figcaption></figure>
<figure class="guide-figure"><a class="pop"><img src="www/gseaplot.png" alt="GSEA plot"/></a><figcaption><strong>GSEA plot</strong><br/>The running enrichment score of a term along the ranked gene list.</figcaption></figure>
<figure class="guide-figure"><a class="pop"><img src="www/emapplot.png" alt="Enrichment map"/></a><figcaption><strong>Enrichment map</strong><br/>Terms linked when their gene sets overlap.</figcaption></figure>
<figure class="guide-figure"><a class="pop"><img src="www/cnetplot.png" alt="Category-gene network"/></a><figcaption><strong>Category-gene network</strong><br/>Terms and the genes that drive them, coloured by fold change.</figcaption></figure>
<figure class="guide-figure"><a class="pop"><img src="www/membership.png" alt="Gene membership chart"/></a><figcaption><strong>Gene membership</strong><br/>Which genes the displayed terms share. Click a bar to list them.</figcaption></figure>
<figure class="guide-figure"><a class="pop"><img src="www/pathview.png" alt="Pathview plot"/></a><figcaption><strong>Pathview</strong><br/>Your fold changes drawn onto a KEGG pathway map.</figcaption></figure>
<figure class="guide-figure"><a class="pop"><img src="www/pubmed.png" alt="PubMed trends"/></a><figcaption><strong>PubMed trends</strong><br/>How often the enriched terms appear in the literature over time.</figcaption></figure>
</div>
<p class="guide-sub" style="margin-top:14px;">The KEGG Plots tab offers the same plots for KEGG pathways. The gseGO and gseKEGG tables can be downloaded as well.</p>
<h3>Preparing your results table</h3>
<ul>
<li>A plain-text table, comma or tab delimited (.csv or .txt), with a header row and one gene per row.</li>
<li>A gene identifier column: ENSEMBL, SYMBOL, ENTREZID or another type you can choose as the key type in step 3. The unnamed first column that DESeq2 writes is accepted.</li>
<li>A numeric log2 fold change column, which is the ranking statistic.</li>
<li>Other columns, such as baseMean or pvalue, are allowed and ignored.</li>
</ul>
<div class="guide-grid">
<figure class="guide-figure guide-table"><img src="www/sampleTable.png" alt="Example results table"/><figcaption><strong>Example table</strong><br/>A differential expression table as written by DESeq2.</figcaption></figure>
<div></div>
</div>
<div class="guide-note">Coming from DESeq2 Shiny? The enrichment buttons under its results table open this app with that comparison already loaded, so there is nothing to upload.</div>
<h3>Choosing the terms to plot</h3>
<p>The plot tabs show the top terms by default. To plot specific ones, select their rows in the gseGO or gseKEGG results table first; the plot tabs then use your selection. On the plot tabs, the interactive gene membership chart shows which genes the displayed terms share: click a bar to list its genes.</p>

<h3>Good to know</h3>
<ul>
<li>The organisms offered are the annotation databases installed on this instance.</li>
<li>KEGG analysis uses NCBI Gene IDs; the app converts your identifiers from the key type you chose.</li>
<li>Genes without a fold change are left out of the ranking.</li>
<li><em>Simplify GO results</em> removes redundant GO terms that are very similar to a more significant one.</li>
</ul>
<p>The app follows this <a href="https://learn.gencore.bio.nyu.edu/rna-seq-analysis/gene-set-enrichment-analysis/" target="_blank">gene set enrichment analysis tutorial</a>.</p>
